messages:
kevin-sre: Heads up — grafana / SLO dashboard for gpu-serving latency is noisy. span_count_prom jumped ~5x at 15:07 UTC but p50/p95 tokens look fine. Prometheus shows a huge increase in spans but trace cardinality didn't move as much. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123

sam-runtime: Ugh, that smells like duplicate spans due to gateway retries. If the gateway retries batched payloads and the exporter isn't deduping by trace_id/span_id we get counted twice. Quick check: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/otel-gateway | grep "retry"

anya-platform: We had a brief Redis flapping window in the same interval (conn resets around 15:05). exporter_queue_depth spiked. If the gateway batches were requeued by the queue layer, they might be re-sent after reconnect.

jessica-ml: Can we confirm by comparing unique trace_id vs total spans? Example quick PromQL to run in Explore: 
```
sum by (job) (rate(otel_span_count_total[5m]))
/
count by (job) (count_values("trace", otel_span_id_total))
```
(not exact metric names here but you get the idea)

kevin-sre: I pulled a small sample from the traces backend — same trace_id appears ~3x with different span_ids and overlapping timestamps. That matches the retry hypothesis. Also saw gateway restarts during the window (ops-bot posted a restart event).

ops-bot: deploy/otel-gateway restarted at 2026-02-28T15:06:42Z due to liveness probe flapping. See incident log #INC-4821.

sam-runtime: Two quick mitigations: 1) change Grafana alert to use unique trace cardinality for SLO (dedupe on trace_id) so noise from duplicates doesn't trigger incidents; 2) add a short-term dedupe filter at the gateway exporter: drop spans if we've seen the same (trace_id, span_id) within a 1m window. That should be cheap.

anya-platform: Agreed. Long-term we should make the queue/retry logic idempotent: add a send-token so retried batches carry the same request id and exporter does idempotent writes. Also fix Redis reconnection backoff to avoid requeueing the entire batch.

jessica-ml: For the dashboard change, we can compute pipeline-effect-free rate: count(distinct_over_time(trace_id[5m])) or in traces store, use unique(trace_id) per timeframe. I'll prototype a panel that shows "spans / unique traces" so we can easily see duplication ratio.

kevin-sre: Action items: 
- sam-runtime to push a gateway hotfix with simple in-memory dedupe + config flag (canary 10%) — target today EOD.
- anya-platform to harden redis backoff and monitor exporter_queue_depth — PR by tomorrow.
- jessica-ml to update Grafana alert to use trace-cardinality and add the duplication ratio panel.
- kevin-sre to silence the existing SLO alert until dedupe is live (reduce noise).

sam-runtime: I'll open the PR now, linking logs and a micro-repro in the branch. Quick snippet of the dedupe idea: 
```go
// simple in-memory LRU of seen keys
key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", span.TraceID, span.SpanID)
if seen.Has(key) { return } // drop
seen.Add(key, time.Now())
export(span)
```
Will gate behind a feature flag.

anya-platform: I'll schedule a canary rollout for the gateway patch on the same cluster + add an alert when exporter_queue_depth > 100 for 2m.

kevin-sre: Thanks everyone. If we still see extra spikes after the hotfix, we'll consider dedup downstream in the traces backend as a last resort. For now, triage and deploy the hotfix + Grafana change. :thumbsup:
